findings.title: Built-in adapter caches replay superseded acceptance as current

baseline.result: Original actual Codex, Claude and Grok paths returned revision-1 accepted:true/current:true after revision-2 owner requirements; direct and fresh reads rejected acceptance. Exit zero meant bug reproduced.
valid_controls: current direct and fresh calls accepted false
baseline.additional_demonstration: All three adapters returned cached accepted result after get_acceptance permission was revoked; direct read denied. Target assertion failed on baseline for all 3.

component_record.root_cause: Completed adapter-cache returns bypassed the durable native-call replay validator and current authorization. Native host bridges required replay-boundary forwarding as well.
component_record.repair: Optional bind_application_replay boundary is bound by composition to durable replay_only invocation. All built-in completed successful application cache hits validate original native binding/current authorization/read applicability. Missing native call or underlying idempotent operation rejects before a new effect. Existing action context construction rechecks resume source/destination and selected effective driver. Custom callbacks without the optional boundary retain cache-only semantics.

examined: Codex native call-ID cache (distinct transport request IDs)
Claude MCP connection/request cache and PreToolUse matching
Grok MCP connection/request cache and ACP native association
SessionBridgeHost native adapter cache -> BridgeSessionDriver replay forwarding
Application.invoke_native cached reads and accept_work decisions
Application.call idempotent replay source/destination/effective driver context
generic custom callback and transport-response duplicate caches
exercised: get_acceptance current/changed/permission-revoked through all three adapters
accept_work duplicate after owner revision through all three adapters
cached get_acceptance inside all three native hosts behind FIFO bridge
non-idempotent create_work duplicate and missing native ledger through all three adapters
start_session resume cached with revoked source/destination and restored allow controls through all three adapters
start_session cached with deleted underlying operation through all three adapters

calibration.activation: After passing first and unchanged replay controls, deliberately set adapter._application_replay=None and revise owner requirements; assert cache actually returns original obsolete accepted:true result.
calibration.expected_effect: Retained superseded acceptance exposed as current
calibration.control: Unmodified replay test passes for each protocol; direct current read rejects obsolete acceptance; unrelated timeout error fails assertion and does not count as target detection.

findings.title: Claude can report idle while another callback remains held

baseline.result: Actual Claude hook helper + subprocess + MCP path had held callbacks A and B; after A Stop status became idle while B remained held; after B Stop idle valid. Exit zero meant bug reproduced.

component_record.root_cause: Any Stop overwrote global activity idle, independent of pending turn and callback identity.
component_record.repair: Claude tracks active/completed prompt IDs, anonymous starts, outstanding application tools and uncertainty. Stop retires only its own identified turn. Duplicate identified completion cannot retire another turn; missing/unmatched/ambiguous overlapping completion retains uncertainty. Callback failures retire running tool bookkeeping while preserving uncertainty. Repeated SessionStart retains outstanding work.

examined: generic ACP future completion success and unknown
exercised: two real held callbacks with separate prompt identities
one valid Stop while another callback held
unknown/missing Stop while known prompt held
callback TimeoutError retires tool and leaves unknown

component_record.original_failure: Move work_completed timestamp after challenge submission but before replies; timing false was reported yet every case still passed.
component_record.root_cause: Checker enforced only submission deadline and reported reply ordering without using it in verdict; lexical ISO sorting also misordered differing timezone offsets.
component_record.repair: Require unfinished-work reply strictly before work completion; compare actual timezone-aware instants, with equality insufficient. Normalize all timestamps chronologically. Busy-tool predicate remains submission-during-hold followed by complete exchange; reply may follow hold release.

Completion and reply timestamps equal
Work start timezone offset places actual start after completion

unaffected_controls: Busy reply after released hold passes while submission inside hold remains required
component_record.independent_challenge: ../independent-checker-challenge/first timezone-start-after-completion passed before fix; qualified unchanged replay rejects.

findings.repair_summary: Unfinished-work replies must precede completion by actual timestamp instant; busy-tool submission semantics remain unchanged.
